title: Research Wiki Frontmatter
description: Frontmatter schema for knowledge/**/*.md pages in research projects using the research-superpowers plugin. Single source of truth — consumed by scripts/lint-wiki.py and VS Code yaml.schemas, referenced by skills.

type.description: Page type. entity = person/place/artefact/institution; concept = theory/method/term; source = cited work; synthesis = cross-source argument.

created.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Set once at creation.

updated.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Bump on every substantive edit.

status.description: draft = being written; review = structurally complete, awaits human check; stable = human-reviewed, citable. Only the user sets stable — agents must not self-promote.

author.description: Who produced the content. human = user; llm = unreviewed LLM; mixed = LLM draft + human edits.

bibkey.description: BibTeX citation key. Required when type = source; matches the entry in output/bibtex/references.bib. Shape: surname-year-shorttitle (e.g. finkelstein-2003-low-chronology), all lowercase ASCII. This is a cross-project JOIN KEY — wiki-global-graph.py matches sources across projects on it — so it must be a deterministic function of the work's own metadata, not a per-project choice: the same work must yield the same key everywhere. It is also the PDF filename stem in the shared library (<library>/pdf/<bibkey>.pdf), so bibkey == PDF stem is a checkable invariant. Add a disambiguation letter after the year for same-author-same-year clashes (finkelstein-2003b-...).

based_on.description: Provenance of the ingested text for type=source. original = the cited work itself (default; field may be omitted); review/preprint/prior-version = a user-approved substitute ingested because the original could not be acquired. Replace with original on re-ingest of the original. Set by ingest-source; see its 'Provenance of substitutes' section.

original_unavailable.description: Optional, type=source only. Declares that NO PDF OF THIS WORK CAN EXIST — not that one has not been acquired yet. It exempts the page from lint-wiki.py's NO-ORIGINAL gate, which otherwise assumes every bibkey resolves to <library>/pdf/<bibkey>.pdf. That assumption is right for articles and wrong for a printed monograph on the shelf or an HTML-only publication. The exemption is NOT silence: the linter counts and reports declared exceptions, because a wiki carrying forty of them is telling you something about its evidence base. Do NOT use it for a paywalled PDF you have not fetched (that belongs in input/bibliography/acquisition-todo.md), for a forthcoming work (the page is premature), or for a substitute you actually read (that is `based_on`).

form.description: physical = a print work read from a physical copy (monograph, offprint) with no digital edition available to you. html-only = published online in HTML with no PDF issued by the publisher (e.g. Internet Archaeology) — note that a browser print-to-PDF does not carry the publication's pagination, so cite by section, not by printed page.

note.description: Why no PDF can exist, and how the cited passages remain checkable — e.g. which edition you read, whether the used chapters were scanned, or which section numbers the citations use. A bare 'is a book' is not enough: the point of the original is that someone can re-check a quotation.

hypothesis.description: Linked hypothesis slug from the research plan. Used on type = synthesis.

bibliography.description: Relative path to the project's BibTeX file (typically ../../output/bibtex/references.bib). Optional; only needed if a page is rendered standalone via Quarto. In the plain-Markdown wiki, citations resolve when the page is pulled into output/.

methodology.description: Optional override for project-level methodology. Drives whether pre-registration gates apply. Defaults to the project-level setting in the root CLAUDE.md frontmatter.

wikidata_qid.description: Wikidata entity ID (e.g. Q173799 for Tel Megiddo, Q483639 for cloud computing). The PRIMARY cross-project join key on both type=entity and type=concept — Wikidata covers named entities and concepts alike, where getty_aat_id (art/architecture/heritage only) does not. Resolvable via dao-paper-search-mcp resolve_author / resolve_site, or wikidata.org.

idai_gazetteer_id.description: iDAI.gazetteer ID (e.g. 2048473). Used on type=entity for archaeological places. Resolvable via dao-paper-search-mcp resolve_site.

gnd_id.description: GND (Gemeinsame Normdatei) authority record (e.g. 118533533). Used on type=entity for persons in German-language scholarship.

orcid.description: ORCID iD (e.g. 0000-0002-1825-0097). Used on type=entity for living researchers — the authority key that actually covers working scientists (where GND / Wikidata often do not), so it is the reliable cross-project join key for method / software papers. Bare iD, no URL. Resolvable via dao-paper-search resolve_author (orcid field) or orcid.org.

getty_aat_id.description: Getty AAT (Art & Architecture Thesaurus) subject ID (e.g. 300054327 for 'archaeology'). OPTIONAL on type=concept, layered on top of the wikidata_qid join key: it adds the curated art/architecture/heritage thesaurus (with its broader/narrower hierarchy) where a precise AAT term exists. AAT is heritage-only — most modern / DH / method concepts have no term (measured: 2 of 19 in one project), so wikidata_qid is the primary key and this is a bonus, not the default. Quote the bare 9-digit iD ('300xxxxxx') so YAML keeps it a string, not an integer. Look up at vocab.getty.edu/aat.

relations.description: Optional structured, confidence-tagged relations to other wiki pages. Complements free-text wikilinks and makes relation type and confidence machine-readable; consumed by scripts/wiki-to-graph.py and validated by scripts/lint-wiki.py. Pages without this field remain valid.

target.description: Target page slug (filename without extension), e.g. finkelstein-2003. Must resolve to an existing knowledge page (checked by lint-wiki.py).

type.description: Relation type. Free vocabulary; common values: cites, contradicts, builds-on, mentions, supports.

confidence.description: extracted = explicitly supported by the source (e.g. verbatim quote with page); inferred = added by the model; ambiguous = relation unclear. The inferred+ambiguous share is reported as the inference-rate by lint-wiki.py.

because.description: Optional one-line rationale for the relation (why A relates to B), ideally with a quote or page reference. Recorded per edge, shown in the graph viz and queries; the natural place to ground an inferred relation when hardening it to extracted.

review_flags.description: Optional single-page content-review findings, raised by the semantic-wiki-review skill (or a human reviewer). A DISTINCT axis from `status` and from `relations`: `status` is human-owned maturity (draft/review/stable) and is never touched by a review; `relations: contradicts` records a conflict BETWEEN two pages; `review_flags` records a concern about THIS page's own content (an overstatement, a weakly-supported claim, a stale assertion). A page can be `status: stable` AND carry an open flag — that is the important case (a blessed page a newer source now undercuts). An `open` flag gates drafting: `drafting-manuscript` will not draft from the page without a logged override, and `wiki-lint` surfaces open flags (it does not fail CI on them). Cleared/kept for audit via `state: resolved`, not by deletion. Pages without this field remain valid.

kind.description: The class of concern. overstatement = epistemic overreach (claim stronger than the source supports); weak-support = assertion without a resolving [[source]] / @citekey; stale = superseded or complicated by a newer ingest; missing-citation = a claim that needs a citation it lacks; open-question = an unresolved point flagged for the author.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the concern, ideally quoting the flagged claim. Recommended — it is what makes the flag actionable without re-reading the audit report.

raised_by.description: Who raised the flag: 'semantic-wiki-review' for the content-audit skill, or a human reviewer's name/handle.

detected.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD when the flag was raised.

state.description: open = unresolved; gates drafting and is surfaced by lint. resolved = addressed; kept as an audit trail rather than deleted.

resolved.description: Optional ISO YYYY-MM-DD when the flag moved to state=resolved.
